questions.prompt: How would you be able to distinguish Class 5 nouns from those in other classes also beginning with "i"? Use the following examples in your answer: intama, ibuye, ijambo, impamvu.
questions.answer: Concerning intama: Class 5 nouns generally do not have in- as their prefix; furthermore in the plural the prefix becomes ama-. Exceptional Class 5 nouns would be those like isahane whose plural is amasahane. There is no separate plural form for intama. Thus intama must be a Class 3 noun. questions.prompt: What is the Law of Dissimilation? How does it operate in such words as igiti, igitabo, gusoma, gushaka?
questions.answer: No two unvoiced consonants can be in juxtaposition. Before unvoiced initial consonants in words such as ikitabo and kusoma, the k- changes to g-, thus: igiti, igitabo, and gusoma.

questions.prompt: This book; these trees. Does the Law of Dissimilation operate in these examples?
questions.answer: It does in the word igitabo, but not with ibi biti, not only because of the value of the initial consonant of the noun, but the demonstrative adjective ibi does not change down any way.
